evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: docs/billing/todo.md has a Resolve first list with three open items on it and I can't start Phase 7 until they're sorted — work through them with me
evals.expected_output: plan-unblock loads, runs resolve_scope.py rather than reading the section by eye, reports each entry as a decision or a person's job with the phase it blocks, probes the repo where a timeboxed read would answer one, puts the rest to the user with a recommendation, and ticks each resolved entry with a Resolved: line naming what settled it.

evals.name: routing-triggers-short-form
evals.prompt: what's actually still blocking us on this plan, and can we close any of it today?
evals.expected_output: plan-unblock loads, discovers the plan, and answers from the script's output — which entries are outstanding, which phases they block, which are already moot because the phase got built anyway.

evals.name: routing-excludes-plan-run
evals.prompt: build the rest of docs/billing/todo.md — every phase that's still unticked
evals.expected_output: Building the plan is plan-run's job; plan-unblock must not load, because it builds nothing and only writes inside the Resolve first section.

evals.name: routing-excludes-spec-design
evals.prompt: now that we've settled the Debezium question, re-plan docs/billing/todo.md around a polling fallback
evals.expected_output: Re-phasing a plan is spec-design's job; plan-unblock must not load, because it never renumbers a phase, regenerates the wave table or rewrites the graph.

evals.name: routing-excludes-plan-run-merge-conflicts
evals.prompt: phase 6 and phase 7 both touched PayoutService and the merge is conflicted — resolve it
evals.expected_output: A conflicted merge is plan-run's --auto-resolve and merge-resolve.py; plan-unblock must not load, despite sharing the word, because it settles open questions in a plan document and touches no git merge state.

evals.name: a-signature-is-never-closed-by-an-interview
evals.expected_output: The entry 'Sign the payments DPA' is classified person and stays OPEN. --yes takes the recommendation on every decision and reaches none of the person entries: nothing closes one but the user saying it is done. The run reports it as still outstanding rather than ticking it and moving on.

evals.name: no-human-halts-instead-of-defaulting
evals.expected_output: With no human able to answer — an unattended session — the run records blocked: 'no-human', ticks nothing and stops. It does NOT fall through to the recommendation: 'I don't know' from the user is an answer and takes the default, but silence is not one, and a default written into the plan as settled is the lie this section exists to prevent.

evals.name: an-unclassified-entry-fails-closed-to-person
evals.expected_output: An entry matching no pattern comes back kind: unclassified and is presented as a person's job, not as a decision — and the run says out loud that it could not classify it, so the user can correct a real decision no pattern matched. The fail-closed direction is the one that cannot close paperwork by asking a model.

evals.name: a-legacy-bullet-is-migrated-not-read-as-settled
evals.expected_output: An entry written as a plain '- **Name** — ...' bullet with no checkbox reads as OUTSTANDING and is rewritten into the checkbox form, with the count reported. It is never read as resolved: that reading would close every pre-existing entry in every plan at once, silently, on the first run.

evals.name: the-plan-is-written-only-inside-its-own-section
evals.expected_output: Resolving an entry ticks that entry and adds its Resolved: line, and changes nothing else in the plan — no phase item, no phase heading, no ## Waves, no renumbering — then commits the plan file alone on base. A '- [ ]' inside a phase block belongs to /r:plan-run, which ticks it after a review that verified it.

evals.name: a-blocker-on-a-built-phase-is-moot-not-a-halt
evals.expected_output: An open entry whose Blocks: names a phase that is already built is reported as moot up front, with an offer to close it on that basis. It does not trap the run, and the skill does not silently tick it either — the script names it, the user closes it.

evals.name: entries-are-briefed-and-taken-one-at-a-time
evals.expected_output: With three open entries, they are worked in document order as R1, R2, R3 — one raised, briefed and settled before the next appears, never all three questions in one message. Each brief is written in Simplified Technical English and in the plan's own nouns: one idea per sentence, active voice, the class and entity names the phase block already uses. It opens with why it blocks, read from the blocked phase's items and Done when: rather than asserted, then at least two options with what each costs, then a recommendation. It is shorter and clearer, not shorter and blunter — it supplies the premise the reader is missing rather than clipping words. A person entry is briefed in its place in the walk, with no options, and closed by nobody.
